gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold entry bundles two independently diagnosable defects in the suboptimality proof: reversed inequality directions and use of an optimal-trajectory time for an approximate-feedback calculation. ISSUE-003 independently diagnoses the sign and value-bound failure, while ISSUE-004 independently diagnoses the incompatible integration time and missing feedback tail control.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both selected predictions establish that the advertised two-sided value and control-cost estimates do not follow: ISSUE-003 covers the sign/orientation failure, and ISSUE-004 covers the mismatch between the optimal stopping time and the approximate closed-loop trajectory together with the unbounded or uncontrolled accumulated residual.
gold_decisions.uncovered_gold_detail: No substantive gold concern remains unrecognised; the demonstrations differ because the two entries diagnose distinct proof defects bundled in the gold issue.
gold_decisions.combination_explanation: The gold issue contains distinct defects: the differential inequality and value estimate have the wrong orientation, and the proof integrates along an approximate trajectory while defining T from the optimal trajectory. ISSUE-003 self-containedly diagnoses the first defect; ISSUE-004 self-containedly diagnoses the second and its tail/infinite-horizon consequence.

component_coverage.gold_component: The differential inequality is integrated with the wrong sign, so the displayed upper bound and resulting two-sided estimate do not follow.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue bundles two independently diagnosable failures in the stability theorem: detectability does not imply the required quadratic coercivity, and the advertised eigenvalue-ratio rate is unsupported. gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The selected entries jointly show that the stated assumptions do not establish the claimed local exponential-stability result or its quantitative rate: ISSUE-006 refutes the coercivity step, while ISSUE-007 refutes the universal P-only rate bound.
gold_decisions.uncovered_gold_detail: No substantive gold concern remains unrecognised; the predictions use different counterexamples and proof steps for the two independent defects.
gold_decisions.combination_explanation: The gold concern has two distinct components. ISSUE-006 self-containedly provides a positive-definite P with q lacking quadratic coercivity, invalidating the decay inference. ISSUE-007 self-containedly provides an exact scalar solution whose rate is below the claimed eigenvalue-ratio bound, invalidating the quantitative rate claim.

component_coverage.gold_component: Detectability and a positive-definite Lyapunov/Riccati matrix do not imply q(x) is bounded below by a positive quadratic near the origin.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-006 supplies a positive-definite Lyapunov solution and an explicit q with quartic behavior along a direction, directly refuting the asserted coercivity.

component_coverage.gold_component: The proof's quantitative rate beta is not bounded below by the claimed eigenvalue ratio, nor by a universal P-only expression.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-007 gives an exact scalar HJB/LQR construction with rate delta but eigenvalue ratio one, and explains the missing dependence on dynamics and cost scale.

gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The Lyapunov solution is only semidefinite under the stated assumptions, so the claimed positive-definite Hessian and exclusion of the trivial solution are unsupported.
